newsitem.title: Netherlands: FOCUS-Consumer turnaround drives Philips Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Consumer turnaround drives Philips Q1 profit.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Wednesday first quarter ordinary net profit jumped 22 percent to 460 million guilders ($239 million) as its consumer products unit swung into profit.
"The first-quarter results provide us with the confidence that we are on track following the improvement programme started in 1996," Philips said in a statement.
Investors cheered the figures, pushing the shares up 9.60 guilders to a new high of 100.70 in early trade on a buoyant Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
"The results looked very good indeed," one dealer commented.

Total first-quarter net profit mushroomed to 887 million guilders from a year-earlier 692 million, lifted by a 427 million guilder one-off gain from the partial flotation of Philips' stake in semiconductors equipment maker ASM Lithography.
Philips consumer products unit turned in a 206 million guilder operating profit, reversing a 52 million guilder loss last year.

The electronics giant said deconsolidation of its German consumer electronics affiliate Grundig, hit by heavy losses in 1996, and better operating performances in sound and vision and domestic appliances had boosted the unit.
The electronics giant said earlier this year it would no longer absorb all of the losses at Grundig in its own results.
Instead it would become a passive minority shareholder, booking Grundig's results under income from unconsolidated companies in proportion to Philips' 32 percent stake.
However, Philips semiconductors, one of the main profit generators in recent years, saw operating income slip to 429 million guilders from a year-earlier 496 million.
Philips said sales had stagnated year-on-year, but added "this reflects an upward trend in performance compared with the fourth quarter of 1996."
Analysts' initial reactions to the ordinary net profit figure -- which came in well ahead of consensus expectations 366 million guilders -- were positive, albeit cautious.
"We are extremely pleased with this result and the progress that has been booked in this first quarter," ING Barings' Steven Vrolijk said.

But Delta Lloyd Bank's Peter Wortel was less upbeat. "Looking simply at the figures, it's good," he said. "Looking deeper...we had expected semiconductors to do better. In fact they're lower." ($ = 1.925 Dutch Guilders)
